DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is a necessary condition for the achievement of productive efficiency?

options.B: the elimination of all divergences between private and social costs
options.C: equality between price and marginal cost in all industries
options.D: the production of a good at minimum average cost for a given output

options.D: The indifference curves for perfect substitutes are right-angled.

options.B: creation of barriers to entry and non-price competition

options.B: a fall in the marginal propensity to import
options.C: an increase in the average propensity to consume
options.D: a reduction in the level of defence expenditure

questions.questionText: An increase in government expenditure is financed by borrowing from the central bank. Other things being equal, what will be the effect on the money supply?

options.B: It will increase by an amount equal to the increase in government expenditure.
options.C: It will increase by more than the increase in government expenditure.

questions.questionText: Which combination of policy measures is most likely to reduce unemployment?

options.A: lowering both the exchange rate and domestic interest rates
options.B: lowering the exchange rate and increasing direct taxation
options.C: raising both the exchange rate and domestic interest rates
options.D: raising the exchange rate and increasing direct taxation

questions.questionText: A government responds to cyclical fluctuations in output by keeping tax rates and benefit rates unchanged. What is the government seeking to achieve by adopting this fiscal policy?

options.A: to allow automatic stabilisers to work
options.B: to keep output at the full employment level
options.C: to maintain a constant balanced budget
options.D: to ensure that its budget is in surplus over the trade cycle
